references.text: The continuation of the law concerning oxen that injure each other, specifying what happens if the ox was known to have gored previously.
Earlier laws in the same chapter about oxen that gore people, establishing the principle of an owner's liability for their livestock's actions.
Laws regarding compensation when livestock cause damage to another's property, illustrating the broader principle of responsibility for harm caused by one's own animals.
The principle of compensation for killed animals, where the one who kills an animal must make restitution.
Solomon's proverbs about fair division and avoiding strife, reflecting the principle of equal sharing between parties.
Complementary rules in the same legal code that distinguish between compensation for property damage and immunity from punishment for unintentional killing.
Expands on the principle in 21:35 by showing that an owner's knowledge of danger changes the penalty from restitution to capital punishment.
The general principle statement (life for life) in Lev 24:21 supports and contextualizes the specific rule of compensation in Ex 21:35.
